answer:
**Embedding migration is a consistency problem as well as a computation problem.** Query vectors from a new encoder may not be compatible with old item vectors. Switching only one side can silently destroy retrieval even if dimensions match. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.08281) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320)

Build a versioned replacement index beside the old one. Backfill in checkpointed jobs, dual-write new updates, and reconcile deletions during the migration. Keep stable document IDs so results and evaluations remain comparable.

**Switch the encoder and index together.** Evaluate judged relevance and slice recall, canary traffic, and retain a rollback path. Account for temporary double storage and embedding throughput across 500 million records.

A learned alignment can sometimes bridge spaces related approximately by rotation, but different semantic geometry cannot be repaired by assuming such a map. Low average alignment error also does not guarantee the same nearest neighbors. Validate retrieval directly. Treat the bridge as a measured migration option, not a substitute for versioning, freshness, and end-to-end consistency.

**Technical details and references.**

For 500 million embeddings, build a new versioned index alongside the old one. Backfill with checkpointed jobs, dual-write document updates, maintain stable document IDs, and compare retrieval on held-out queries. Switch query encoder and index version atomically, canary traffic, retain rollback, then retire the old index after verification. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.08281) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320)

A learned alignment can provide a temporary bridge: fit an orthogonal map on paired old/new embeddings if their geometry is approximately related by rotation. Different dimensions or changed semantic structure violate that assumption; a low alignment error alone does not establish retrieval recall. Evaluate top-k overlap, judged relevance, and slices. Account for peak storage, embedding throughput, deletions during backfill, and consistency rather than assuming migration is only an offline matrix multiplication.
